skill.name: check-product-segments
skill.description: Review ecommerce ad performance across six Product Metrics segments. See segment revenue and return on ad spend, find products by segment, and review how classifications changed without changing store settings.
skill.summary: Review product segment performance, Drainer spend, and classification history in Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown labels, documentation links, or scoped reporting operations, not shell substitution or host reconnaissance. The SQL fallback passes generated text to a shell command without specifying safe argument handling. The CLI preview stages store settings locally, and the workflow can query a connected store without first confirming that the user intends to use it.

remediation.issue: The general SQL fallback passes generated query text to the CLI without specifying a safe invocation or a narrow data scope.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the fallback with predefined read-only reports scoped to the selected property. If retained, use an argument-vector API and enforce read-only queries and property scope server-side.

remediation.issue: The CLI preview saves store settings to a fixed local filename without cleanup instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid writing settings to disk if possible. Otherwise create a private temporary file without overwriting existing files, and remove it after the preview, including on failure.

remediation.issue: The skill can infer permission to access a connected store from a product question alone.
remediation.suggestion: Before reading store metrics, confirm the Product Metrics connection and property when the user's request has not already authorized that scope.

content.user_title: Review Product Segments and Ad Spend
content.value_statement: Store totals can hide which product groups drive revenue and which consume ad budget without profit. Review segment performance and classification changes for a connected Product Metrics store.
actual_capabilities: Summarize product counts, revenue, revenue share, and return on ad spend across the six Product Metrics segments.
Report how much ad budget goes to Drainers and rank the products in that segment by spend.
List products in a selected segment and sort them by conversion value or spend.
Look up a product's segment changes and compare its results seven days before and after each move.
Compare weekly segment trends and report week-over-week changes for products with daily history.
Read which Merchant Center custom label carries the segment assignments.
limitations: Requires a connected Product Metrics store. Some reports require Product Segmentation or Pro.
Product-level segment lists and classification history require the MCP connection.
Segment totals use the configured reporting window. Weekly change reports cover only products with daily history.
Segments describe past performance. The skill does not predict profit or change store settings, product rules, or campaigns.

use_cases.title: Review where ad spend goes
use_cases.description: See how much budget Drainers used and which products account for the most spend.

use_cases.title: Investigate a product move
use_cases.description: Use a product's segment history to compare results around its move out of Stars. Note any settings changes reported near that date.

use_cases.title: Prepare a weekly segment report
use_cases.description: Compare two weeks by segment and show how much spend the daily history covers.

prompt_templates.title: Review segment performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize the six Product Metrics segments for [store]. Include product counts, revenue, return on ad spend, and the reporting dates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Review the configured reporting period.

prompt_templates.title: Find the largest Drainer expenses
prompt_templates.prompt: How much ad spend went to Drainers in [store]? List the five highest-spend products and include the date range and currency.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Identify products to review first.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a move out of Stars
prompt_templates.prompt: When did [product] in [store] leave Stars? Compare results seven days before and after the move. Note nearby settings changes without assuming they caused it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Explain a product classification change.

prompt_templates.title: Compare weekly segment changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the latest two reported weeks for [store] by segment. State each week's dates and spend coverage. Identify the largest changes and the products behind them.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Compare periods and account for partial coverage.

output_examples.input: How much did Drainers cost the North Shop?
output_examples.output: From June 1 to June 30, North Shop spent USD 420 on Drainers, or 12% of its ad spend. The highest-spend Drainer was the Canvas Tote at USD 95.

output_examples.input: Why did the Trail Jacket leave Stars in the North Shop?
output_examples.output: The Trail Jacket moved from Stars to Question Marks on June 12. Its return on ad spend was 4.6 in the seven days before and 3.2 in the seven days after. The history does not establish why it moved.

best_practices: Name the Product Metrics store before requesting a report, especially if several stores are connected.
Include the reporting dates and account currency when sharing spend or revenue.
State the spend covered by weekly comparisons and separate observed changes from possible causes.
anti_patterns: Treating a segment label as a forecast of future profit.
Using weekly figures for products with daily history as if they represented the whole store.
Asking the skill to change campaigns, product rules, or segmentation settings.

faq.question: What are the six product segments?
faq.answer: Product Metrics uses Stars, Question Marks, Cash Cows, Dogs, Drainers, and Ghosts. It considers profitability and potential, while Ghosts are inactive and have no impressions.

faq.question: What do I need to connect?
faq.answer: Connect your store through the Product Metrics MCP integration or CLI. Product-level segment lists and history require MCP.

faq.question: Does this skill change campaigns or store settings?
faq.answer: No. It reports findings and can suggest options, but it does not apply changes to campaigns, settings, or rules.

faq.question: Can it tell me why a product changed segments?
faq.answer: It shows the transition, performance around it, and nearby settings changes. Those observations do not prove what caused the move.

faq.question: Which dates are used for the totals?
faq.answer: Segment totals use the date range configured in Product Segmentation. Weekly changes cover only products with daily history.

faq.question: Why is a report unavailable?
faq.answer: Some reports require a Product Segmentation or Pro subscription. The skill relays the requirement reported by the connected tool.
